front.title: Causal Diagnostics for Semantic Drift in Autonomous Agent Communications: Counterfactual Testing, Source-Role Separation, and Evidence-Bounded Handoff Localization

abstract.t:
Multi-agent AI systems pass instructions, facts and tool outputs through summaries, translations, delegations and protocol conversions. When a downstream proposed operation departs from the originating instruction, existing records may show that a message was sent, authenticated or traced, yet not show whether a lower-trust source's instruction-like statement influenced a governing condition, whether an intermediary dropped the condition, or whether the receiver misapplied it. This document describes a diagnostic architecture, and an optional transport-neutral evidence model, for investigating such semantic drift. It uses typed originating task contracts, condition-scoped source roles, versioned dependency graphs, handoff lineage, matched counterfactual tests that vary legitimate facts and unauthorized instruction-like content separately, adaptive witness selection, uncertainty-aware comparison, and evidence-bounded localization that reports an earliest observable divergence, a bounded interval, or abstains.
The architecture is diagnostic only. It does not grant, veto or finalize any execution; authorization stays with separate systems. The document is an individual, informational proposal; it makes no novelty, compliance, adoption or performance claim, and reports no experimental results beyond those the underlying filing itself states.
